title: Modernization without a common starting point

blocks.text: Modern facilities and political autonomy are different things. A colony could possess railways, courts, schools and administrative records without deciding whose purposes they served. Similar forms could contain very different relations of power.

Colonial modernity in India requires precisely this distinction between capability and control. The arrival of modern institutions did not place those controlling and using them in equal positions. Transport and education alone did not establish conditions for autonomous development.

Latin American independence likewise did not automatically erase histories of land, exports and social relationships. African societies entering colonial arrangements also possessed different prior structures and connections; they were not one uniform space undergoing an identical process.

Modernization therefore had no common starting point. Independent states, reforming empires and colonial societies entered global systems differently. Comparison must ask who directed institutions, received benefits and bore costs, rather than merely count modern facilities.
